name: Every operator and verifier list change is audited
summary: operators/verifiers add|remove take --actor/--reason; restore-new too. A change appends an entry to authority-changes.audit.json (0600, 200 kept) under the lock before the configuration. Every NEW history begins with a baseline of the lists as they stood; an unreadable one is null (UNKNOWN). An ADD that would start a history while a list cannot be read is refused; a REMOVAL never is, for the audit or the OTHER list: it records null and goes on. authority-changes: replay.agrees is false when ANY comparable list disagrees, beside an unreadable one; null (incomplete) when one was not compared, or no trail. authority-changes-baseline records the reader's verdict on the replaced history (state, unexplained names per list, kept name), prints a WARNING, lists .replaced-* under replaced_files, and REFUSES a mismatch or damaged history without --accept-unexplained; an incomplete/null one needs no flag and the cap fold carries the note. A damaged audit never refuses a REMOVAL: the bytes go beside it first. Placeholders are refused on an ADD (re-checked under the lock), dropped on a REMOVAL, recorded unattributed. NOT covered: a hand edit of deployment.private.json; a change by an older kit.
